# CBACT04C — Program Specification

## Overview

CBACT04C is a batch interest calculator for the CardDemo credit-card application. It reads the transaction-category balance file (`TCATBAL-FILE`) in key sequence — one record per account / transaction-type / transaction-category combination — and for each record looks up the owning account, its card cross-reference, and the interest rate that applies to that account's disclosure group for that transaction type and category. Where a non-zero rate applies, it computes one month's interest on that category balance, writes an interest transaction record to the output transaction file, and accumulates the interest into a running per-account total. When the account number changes from one input record to the next, the accumulated interest for the *previous* account is added to that account's current balance and the account record is rewritten with its current-cycle credit and debit amounts reset to zero. The driver logic sits directly in the `PROCEDURE DIVISION` body (there is no named `MAIN` paragraph): it opens all five files, runs a `PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'` loop over the balance file, then closes all five files and returns via `GOBACK`. The program is invoked with a linkage parameter (`EXTERNAL-PARMS`) whose `PARM-DATE` supplies the prefix of every generated transaction ID.

## Paragraph flow

### 0000-TCATBALF-OPEN
Called first by the driver. Sets `APPL-RESULT` to 8, opens `TCATBAL-FILE` for INPUT, and sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0 when `TCATBALF-STATUS = '00'`, otherwise 12. If the result is not the "AOK" condition (`APPL-RESULT = 0`), it displays `'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION CATEGORY BALANCE'`, moves the file status into `IO-STATUS`, and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0100-XREFFILE-OPEN
Same open-and-check pattern for `XREF-FILE` (OPEN INPUT). On failure displays `'ERROR OPENING CROSS REF FILE'` together with `XREFFILE-STATUS`, then calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0200-DISCGRP-OPEN
Same pattern for `DISCGRP-FILE` (OPEN INPUT). On failure displays `'ERROR OPENING DALY REJECTS FILE'` — the message text does not match the file being opened, which is a cosmetic defect in the legacy source, not a behavioural one. Calls: `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0300-ACCTFILE-OPEN
Opens `ACCOUNT-FILE` **I-O** (read/update), not INPUT, because the program rewrites account records later. Same status check; on failure displays `'ERROR OPENING ACCOUNT MASTER FILE'` and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 0400-TRANFILE-OPEN
Opens `TRANSACT-FILE` **OUTPUT** — the transaction file is created fresh on every run, so any prior contents are replaced. Same status check; on failure displays `'ERROR OPENING TRANSACTION FILE'` and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT
Sequentially reads the next transaction-category balance record into `TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD`. Status `'00'` sets `APPL-RESULT` to 0; status `'10'` (end of file) sets it to 16, which satisfies the `APPL-EOF` condition and causes `'Y'` to be moved to `END-OF-FILE`; any other status sets 12 and produces `'ERROR READING TRANSACTION CATEGORY FILE'` followed by `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Called from the driver loop; on a successful read the driver adds 1 to `WS-RECORD-COUNT` and displays the whole `TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD`.

### 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT
Posts the accumulated interest to the account currently held in `ACCOUNT-RECORD`:

```
ADD WS-TOTAL-INT  TO ACCT-CURR-BAL
MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT
MOVE 0 TO ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT
REWRITE FD-ACCTFILE-REC FROM  ACCOUNT-RECORD
```

In plain English: the total interest computed for all of that account's category balances is added to the account's current balance, and both current-cycle credit and debit accumulators are zeroed, then the account record is rewritten in place. A rewrite status other than `'00'` produces `'ERROR RE-WRITING ACCOUNT FILE'` and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Called from the driver when the account ID on the newly-read record differs from `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` and this is not the first record of the run.

### 1100-GET-ACCT-DATA
Random-reads `ACCOUNT-FILE` on key `FD-ACCT-ID` (which the driver has just loaded from `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID`) into `ACCOUNT-RECORD`. An `INVALID KEY` branch displays `'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: '` with the key, but execution then falls into the status check, where any status other than `'00'` displays `'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE'` and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM` — so a missing account aborts the run rather than being skipped.

### 1110-GET-XREF-DATA
Random-reads `XREF-FILE` into `CARD-XREF-RECORD` using the alternate key `FD-XREF-ACCT-ID` to obtain the card number for the account. Same `INVALID KEY` display (`'ACCOUNT NOT FOUND: '`) followed by the same abort-on-non-`'00'` status check with message `'ERROR READING XREF FILE'`. Called by the driver immediately after `1100-GET-ACCT-DATA` whenever the account changes.

### 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE
Random-reads `DISCGRP-FILE` into `DIS-GROUP-RECORD` using the key built by the driver from `ACCT-GROUP-ID`, `TRANCAT-TYPE-CD` and `TRANCAT-CD`. `INVALID KEY` displays `'DISCLOSURE GROUP RECORD MISSING'` and `'TRY WITH DEFAULT GROUP CODE'`. Statuses `'00'` **or** `'23'` (record not found) are both treated as acceptable (`APPL-RESULT` 0); anything else displays `'ERROR READING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE'` and aborts via `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` / `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. When the status was `'23'`, it moves the literal `'DEFAULT'` into `FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID` and performs `1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE`. Calls: `1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE
Re-reads `DISCGRP-FILE` into `DIS-GROUP-RECORD` with the group ID now set to `'DEFAULT'` (transaction type and category unchanged). Here only status `'00'` is acceptable; any other status displays `'ERROR READING DEFAULT DISCLOSURE GROUP'` and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. In other words, a missing account-specific rate falls back to the DEFAULT group, but a missing DEFAULT-group rate is fatal.

### 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST
Computes one month's interest on the current category balance:

```
COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT
 = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200

ADD WS-MONTHLY-INT  TO WS-TOTAL-INT
```

In plain English: the category balance is multiplied by the annual percentage rate and divided by 1200 — 100 to convert the percentage to a fraction, 12 to convert the annual rate to a monthly one — giving the month's interest, which is then accumulated into the per-account running total. There is no `ROUNDED` phrase, so the result is truncated to the two decimal places of `WS-MONTHLY-INT` (`S9(09)V99`, BigDecimal precision 11 scale 2). Then performs `1300-B-WRITE-TX`. Called by the driver only when `DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0`.

### 1300-B-WRITE-TX
Builds and writes one interest transaction record. It adds 1 to `WS-TRANID-SUFFIX` and builds the transaction ID by concatenation:

```
STRING PARM-DATE,
       WS-TRANID-SUFFIX
  DELIMITED BY SIZE
  INTO TRAN-ID
```

— the 10-character run date from the linkage parameter followed by the 6-digit sequence number, exactly filling `TRAN-ID` (`X(16)`). It then sets `TRAN-TYPE-CD` to `'01'`, `TRAN-CAT-CD` to `'05'`, `TRAN-SOURCE` to `'System'`, and builds the description by concatenating the literal `'Int. for a/c '` with `ACCT-ID`. `WS-MONTHLY-INT` is moved to `TRAN-AMT`, merchant ID is set to 0 and the three merchant text fields to spaces, `XREF-CARD-NUM` (from the cross-reference read) is moved to `TRAN-CARD-NUM`, and `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP` is performed so that the resulting `DB2-FORMAT-TS` can be moved into both `TRAN-ORIG-TS` and `TRAN-PROC-TS` (origin and processing timestamps are therefore always identical). The record is written with `WRITE FD-TRANFILE-REC FROM TRAN-RECORD`; a status other than `'00'` displays `'ERROR WRITING TRANSACTION RECORD'` and calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` then `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`. Calls: `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP`, `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 1400-COMPUTE-FEES
A stub. Its entire body is the comment `* To be implemented` followed by `EXIT.` It is performed by the driver immediately after `1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST` whenever the rate is non-zero, but does nothing. A Java implementation should reproduce it as an empty extension point, not invent fee logic.

### 9000-TCATBALF-CLOSE
Sets `APPL-RESULT` to 8, closes `TCATBAL-FILE`, sets 0 on status `'00'` else 12, and on failure displays `'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION BALANCE FILE'` then calls `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` and `9999-ABEND-PROGRAM`.

### 9100-XREFFILE-CLOSE
Same close-and-check pattern for `XREF-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING CROSS REF FILE'`.

### 9200-DISCGRP-CLOSE
Same pattern for `DISCGRP-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING DISCLOSURE GROUP FILE'`.

### 9300-ACCTFILE-CLOSE
Same pattern for `ACCOUNT-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE'`.

### 9400-TRANFILE-CLOSE
Same pattern for `TRANSACT-FILE`; failure message `'ERROR CLOSING TRANSACTION FILE'`. After this the driver displays `'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT04C'` and issues `GOBACK`.

### Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP
Moves `FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE` into the `COBOL-TS` structure, then copies the year, month, day, hour, minute, second and hundredths components into the corresponding positions of `DB2-FORMAT-TS`, moves `'0000'` into `DB2-REST`, and inserts `'-'` into the three date separators and `'.'` into the three time separators — producing a 26-character DB2-style timestamp of the shape `YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.HH0000`. Note that the target subfields of `DB2-FORMAT-TS` are defined through a `REDEFINES` and are therefore flagged for human review below; a Java implementation must reproduce the exact 26-character layout, including the trailing `'0000'` padding on the fractional seconds. Called from `1300-B-WRITE-TX`.

### 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM
Displays `'ABENDING PROGRAM'`, moves 0 to `TIMING` and 999 to `ABCODE`, and issues `CALL 'CEE3ABD' USING ABCODE, TIMING` — a Language Environment abend with user code 999 and immediate timing. In Java this is an immediate, non-recoverable termination of the batch job, not a caught exception.

### 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
Formats and displays a four-character file status. If `IO-STATUS` is not numeric or `IO-STAT1 = '9'`, it puts `IO-STAT1` into the first byte of `IO-STATUS-04`, zeroes `TWO-BYTES-BINARY`, moves `IO-STAT2` into `TWO-BYTES-RIGHT` (the low-order byte of the binary halfword via the `REDEFINES`), and moves the resulting binary value into `IO-STATUS-0403` — i.e. it renders the second status byte as its numeric character-code value. Otherwise it moves `'0000'` into `IO-STATUS-04` and overlays the two-character status at positions 3–4. Either branch displays `'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN'` followed by `IO-STATUS-04`. This paragraph depends on `TWO-BYTES-RIGHT`, which is a flagged `REDEFINES` field.

## Business rules

- **Driver loop:** the balance file is processed sequentially until `END-OF-FILE = 'Y'`. Every successfully read record increments `WS-RECORD-COUNT` and is echoed with `DISPLAY TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD`.
- **Account-break detection:** when `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM`, the program (a) posts the previous account via `1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` — unless `WS-FIRST-TIME = 'Y'`, in which case it only flips `WS-FIRST-TIME` to `'N'` and posts nothing; (b) resets `WS-TOTAL-INT` to 0; (c) records the new account in `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM`; and (d) re-reads the account record and cross-reference record for the new account. This break logic assumes the input file is in account-ID order, which the indexed sequential read guarantees.
- **Comparison type mismatch (observation):** `WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM` is `X(11)` while `TRANCAT-ACCT-ID` is `9(11)`; the break test is therefore an alphanumeric comparison of the digit characters. Its initial value is `SPACES`, so the very first record always registers as a break. A Java implementation must reproduce the same "first record always breaks" behaviour.
- **Rate lookup key:** the disclosure-group key is built each iteration from `ACCT-GROUP-ID` (from the account record), `TRANCAT-CD` and `TRANCAT-TYPE-CD` (from the current balance record) — so the group ID is refreshed only on an account break, while type and category are refreshed on every record.
- **Missing rate falls back to DEFAULT:** disclosure-group status `'23'` is not an error; the lookup is retried with group ID `'DEFAULT'`. A failed DEFAULT lookup is fatal (abend).
- **Zero-rate short circuit:** interest is computed and a transaction written **only** when `DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0`. A zero rate produces no transaction record and contributes nothing to `WS-TOTAL-INT`. `1400-COMPUTE-FEES` is likewise only reached on a non-zero rate.
- **Interest formula, verbatim:** `COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200`. No `ROUNDED` clause, so the result is **truncated** (not rounded) to two decimals when stored into `WS-MONTHLY-INT` (`S9(09)V99`). Java must use a truncating scale-2 operation (`RoundingMode.DOWN`), not half-up rounding, and must not round the intermediate product before the division.
- **Posting:** `ADD WS-TOTAL-INT TO ACCT-CURR-BAL`, then `ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT` and `ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT` are both set to 0 before the account record is rewritten. Cycle accumulators are cleared unconditionally as part of the posting step.
- **Transaction record content:** type code `'01'`, category code `'05'`, source `'System'`, description `'Int. for a/c '` + `ACCT-ID`, amount `WS-MONTHLY-INT`, merchant ID 0, merchant name/city/zip spaces, card number from the cross-reference record, and both timestamps set to the same generated DB2-format value.
- **Transaction ID generation:** `PARM-DATE` (10 chars, supplied by the caller) concatenated with a 6-digit counter that increments once per written transaction across the whole run, starting from 000001. IDs are therefore unique within a run only if `PARM-DATE` differs between runs.
- **Output file is recreated:** `TRANSACT-FILE` is opened `OUTPUT`, so each run replaces the file rather than appending.
- **End-of-file handling (observation — the last account is not posted):** the loop is `PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y'` and the `ELSE PERFORM 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT` branch is guarded by `IF END-OF-FILE = 'N'`. Because the loop condition is retested before the body re-executes, once `1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT` sets `END-OF-FILE` to `'Y'` the loop terminates and that `ELSE` branch is never reached. The consequence is that the accumulated `WS-TOTAL-INT` for the **final** account in the file is never added to `ACCT-CURR-BAL` — its interest transactions are written to the transaction file, but the account balance is not updated. This is behaviour of the existing program, not a suggestion; a faithful Java port must decide deliberately whether to reproduce it, and the choice should be raised with a human.
- **Error handling is uniformly fatal:** every I/O status check that fails displays a message, formats the status via `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`, and abends with user code 999. There is no record-level skip-and-continue anywhere in the program — including for a not-found account or cross-reference record, where the `INVALID KEY` display is immediately followed by the fatal status check.

Two distinct fields share the name `FD-ACCT-DATA` (`X(289)` in the account FD, `X(334)` in the transaction FD); Java naming must disambiguate them by record. Note also that `ACCT-GROUP-ID` is `X(10)` while `DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID` is `X(10)` — the `'DEFAULT'` literal moved into `FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID` is space-padded to 10 characters.

## Flagged for human review

These fields were deliberately not mapped, per `docs/adr/0002-a-hand-rolled-parser-for-a-deliberately-bounded-grammar.md`. No Java shape is proposed for any of them.

- **`TWO-BYTES-LEFT`** — declared under `01 TWO-BYTES-ALPHA REDEFINES TWO-BYTES-BINARY`; an alphanumeric overlay of a binary halfword, whose meaning depends on machine byte order and cannot be mapped safely.
- **`TWO-BYTES-RIGHT`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; used by `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS` to reinterpret a status byte as a numeric value, so the display formatting cannot be reproduced until a human decides the byte-level semantics.
- **`DB2-YYYY`** — declared under `01 FILLER REDEFINES DB2-FORMAT-TS`; a positional overlay of the 26-character timestamp string.
- **`DB2-MIN`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay of `DB2-FORMAT-TS`.
- **`DB2-DOT-2`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; a separator position within the timestamp.
- **`DB2-SS`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay of `DB2-FORMAT-TS`.
- **`DB2-DOT-3`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; a separator position within the timestamp.
- **`DB2-MIL`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; numeric `PIC 9(002)` over a slice of an alphanumeric field.
- **`DB2-REST`** — same `REDEFINES` overlay; the trailing four characters of the timestamp, always set to `'0000'`.

All nine flagged fields are consumed by `Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP` or `9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS`. Because the timestamp overlay drives both `TRAN-ORIG-TS` and `TRAN-PROC-TS` on every written transaction record, a human must resolve the timestamp layout before those paragraphs can be ported.

rule_confidence.rule: Driver loop processes TCATBAL-FILE sequentially until END-OF-FILE = 'Y', incrementing WS-RECORD-COUNT and displaying TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD on each successful read.
rule_confidence.rationale: The main PROCEDURE DIVISION loop directly implements this: PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' with ADD 1 TO WS-RECORD-COUNT and DISPLAY TRAN-CAT-BAL-RECORD inside the successful-read branch.

rule_confidence.rule: Account-break detection on TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM triggers UPDATE-ACCOUNT (unless WS-FIRST-TIME = 'Y'), resets WS-TOTAL-INT to 0, records the new account, and re-reads account and cross-reference records.
rule_confidence.rationale: The driver loop explicitly implements this four-step sequence in the IF TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM block, with the first-time guard on 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT.

rule_confidence.rule: WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM is X(11) string initialized to SPACES, so the first record always triggers an account break despite the leading numeric key.
rule_confidence.rationale: WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM is defined as PIC X(11) VALUE SPACES in WS-MISC-VARS. A numeric 9(11) key will never equal SPACES, guaranteeing the first break.

rule_confidence.rule: Interest is computed and a transaction written only when DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0.
rule_confidence.rationale: The driver loop gate is explicitly IF DIS-INT-RATE NOT = 0 PERFORM 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST PERFORM 1400-COMPUTE-FEES END-IF; a zero rate skips both paragraphs and contributes nothing to WS-TOTAL-INT.

rule_confidence.rule: Interest formula is COMPUTE WS-MONTHLY-INT = ( TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200, with the result truncated (not rounded) to 2 decimal places on store to S9(09)V99.
rule_confidence.rationale: The formula in 1300-COMPUTE-INTEREST is verbatim; there is no ROUNDED clause, so COBOL semantics truncate the quotient to the target scale.

rule_confidence.rule: Posted account balance receives ADD WS-TOTAL-INT TO ACCT-CURR-BAL, and ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT are both set to 0 unconditionally.
rule_confidence.rationale: 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT performs all three statements in order: ADD, then MOVE 0 to both cycle accumulators, then REWRITE.

rule_confidence.rule: Generated transaction record has type '01', category '05', source 'System', description 'Int. for a/c ' concatenated with ACCT-ID, amount WS-MONTHLY-INT, merchant ID 0, merchant name/city/zip as spaces, card from cross-reference, and identical timestamps.
rule_confidence.rationale: 1300-B-WRITE-TX explicitly sets each field: MOVE '01' to TRAN-TYPE-CD, MOVE '05' to TRAN-CAT-CD, MOVE 'System' to TRAN-SOURCE, STRING description, set merchant ID to 0, MOVE SPACES to merchant fields, copy XREF-CARD-NUM, call timestamp routine, and move same DB2-FORMAT-TS to both timestamps.

rule_confidence.rule: Transaction ID is built by STRING PARM-DATE (10 characters) + WS-TRANID-SUFFIX (6 digits), exactly filling TRAN-ID (X(16)), with suffix incrementing from 1 per transaction.
rule_confidence.rationale: 1300-B-WRITE-TX adds 1 to WS-TRANID-SUFFIX (initialized to 0, so first is 1), then STRINGs PARM-DATE and the suffix DELIMITED BY SIZE into TRAN-ID (10+6=16 characters).

rule_confidence.rule: TRANSACT-FILE is opened OUTPUT, replacing any prior contents rather than appending.
rule_confidence.rationale: 0400-TRANFILE-OPEN explicitly performs OPEN OUTPUT TRANSACT-FILE; OUTPUT mode truncates the file.

rule_confidence.rule: Final account's accumulated interest is not posted to the account master file, though its interest transactions are written.
rule_confidence.rationale: The loop is PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y', so when 1000-TCATBALF-GET-NEXT sets END-OF-FILE to 'Y', the next condition test exits the loop; the ELSE branch of the IF statement is never reached, and 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT is not performed for the final account.

rule_confidence.rule: All file I/O failures display an error message, call 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, and call 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM with user code 999.
rule_confidence.rationale: Every open, read, and write paragraph (and 1100, 1110, 1200, 1200-A) uses the same pattern: IF APPL-AOK CONTINUE ELSE DISPLAY message, PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS, PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM END-IF.

rule_confidence.rule: Disclosure group status '23' (record not found) is treated as non-fatal; the lookup is retried with group ID set to 'DEFAULT'.
rule_confidence.rationale: 1200-GET-INTEREST-RATE sets APPL-RESULT to 0 if status is '00' OR '23', so only other statuses trigger the error branch. If status = '23', MOVE 'DEFAULT' to FD-DIS-ACCT-GROUP-ID and PERFORM 1200-A-GET-DEFAULT-INT-RATE.

rule_confidence.rule: DB2 timestamp is formatted as YYYY-MM-DD-HH.MM.SS.HH0000 (26 characters).
rule_confidence.rationale: Z-GET-DB2-FORMAT-TIMESTAMP builds DB2-FORMAT-TS via REDEFINES subfields, moving components to YYYY, MM, DD, HH, MIN, SS, MIL, and '0000' to REST, then inserting three dashes and three dots at the specified positions via DB2-STREEP-* and DB2-DOT-* assignments.

rule_confidence.rule: 1400-COMPUTE-FEES is an empty stub consisting only of a comment '* To be implemented' and EXIT.
rule_confidence.rationale: The paragraph body in the source is exactly those two lines; it performs no actual fee calculation.

rule_confidence.rule: File status codes are interpreted such that status '00' always means success; status '10' (end-of-file) sets APPL-RESULT to 16 (APPL-EOF condition); other statuses set APPL-RESULT to 12.
rule_confidence.rationale: All file I/O paragraphs follow the same pattern: IF status = '00' MOVE 0, IF status = '10' MOVE 16, ELSE MOVE 12; APPL-EOF is defined as condition 88 VALUE 16.

rule_confidence.rule: ACCOUNT-FILE is opened I-O (read/write) because the program rewrites account records, unlike the input-only files.
rule_confidence.rationale: 0300-ACCTFILE-OPEN explicitly performs OPEN I-O ACCOUNT-FILE; 1050-UPDATE-ACCOUNT performs REWRITE, confirming the file must be opened for update.

steps.description: Opens the category-balance, cross-reference, disclosure-group, account (I-O) and transaction (OUTPUT, recreated) resources, aborting the job on any status other than '00'.
Reads the transaction-category balance file sequentially in key order, one TranCatBal per item, ending the step on file status '10'.
On an account break, randomly reads the Account by TRANCAT-ACCT-ID and the CardXref by the account alternate key, attaching both to the current category balance.
Looks up the DisGroup rate by ACCT-GROUP-ID / TRANCAT-TYPE-CD / TRANCAT-CD, falling back to the 'DEFAULT' group when the account-specific record is not found (status '23').
Computes (TRAN-CAT-BAL * DIS-INT-RATE) / 1200 truncated to scale 2 as WS-MONTHLY-INT and leaves the fee hook as an empty extension point.

Builds and writes one interest Tran per accrued category — TRAN-ID of PARM-DATE plus a run-wide 6-digit suffix, type '01', category '05', source 'System', amount WS-MONTHLY-INT, card number from the cross-reference, and one DB2-format timestamp in both TRAN-ORIG-TS and TRAN-PROC-TS.
Adds the account's summed WS-TOTAL-INT to ACCT-CURR-BAL, zeroes ACCT-CURR-CYC-CREDIT and ACCT-CURR-CYC-DEBIT, and rewrites the Account record once per account group.
steps.guard_condition: TRANCAT-ACCT-ID NOT= WS-LAST-ACCT-NUM AND WS-FIRST-TIME NOT = 'Y' AND END-OF-FILE = 'N'

steps.description: Closes all five resources in source order, aborting the job on any close status other than '00'.
